name: Aeonik Extended
classification_notes: Wide-set geometric sans-serif with mechanical construction; the extended-width member of the Aeonik superfamily (which also includes Aeonik, Aeonik Condensed, Aeonik Mono and Aeonik Fono). Available as a variable font. Optimised for display and headline use rather than continuous text.
summary: The extended-width member of CoType's Aeonik superfamily, available across seven weights with matching italics for bold headlines and high-presence brand display work.
description: Aeonik Extended widens the geometric construction of the original Aeonik into expanded proportions, producing letterforms with strong horizontal presence and an open, confident feel. Seven weights run from Thin to Black, each paired with an italic, giving 16 styles in total; the family also ships as a variable font for precise weight control within a single file. Language support spans Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese, with OpenType features including old-style figures, tabular numerals, fractions and case-sensitive punctuation.
foundry_blurb: Aeonik Extended stretches the Aeonik geometry into a wider form to create a sense of openness and boldness while keeping the family's characteristic mechanical precision. Eight weights from Thin to Black with matching italics are available, with formats including OTF, TTF and variable fonts, and language options selectable at checkout.

name: RM Neue
classification_notes: Compact neo-grotesque with low contrast and consistent stroke weight. Ascenders match cap height. Default 'l' carries a curly serif to prevent confusion with capital 'I'. OpenType alternates include a single-storey 'a', seriffless 'l', and alternate forms for 'R', 'G' and '3'. Italics are oblique rather than true drawn italics. Variable font available across the weight axis.
summary: A compact neo-grotesque in five weights with oblique italics and a variable axis, built on CoType's RM lineage dating back to 2011.
description: RM Neue is a neo-grotesque sans-serif with compact proportions and low contrast, drawing from utilitarian type traditions. First released as RM in 2011 and fully redesigned in 2019, it spans five weights from Light to Black, each paired with an oblique, plus a variable font for continuous weight adjustment. Considered detailing sets it apart from generic grotesques: the default 'l' carries a curly serif, with OpenType alternates for a single-storey 'a' and alternate 'R', 'G' and '3' forms.
foundry_blurb: CoType positions RM Neue as a timeless and versatile addition to any designer's toolkit, suited to modern websites, zines and minimal layouts. The slightly heavier Regular weight is recommended at 12–16pt for body text, while the full weight range handles display and headline use. It supports Latin Extended A and ships in OTF, WOFF, WOFF2 and variable formats.

name: Aeonik Soft
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque with uniformly softened corners throughout all glyphs. Maintains the mechanical structure and proportions of Aeonik but substitutes hard junctions for gentle curves at every terminal and junction. Sits between a hard geometric grotesque and a fully rounded sans — warmer than the original without becoming decorative.
summary: A softened companion to Aeonik that introduces gently curved corners across the neo-grotesque structure, giving it warmth without losing geometric clarity.
description: Aeonik Soft keeps the mechanical backbone of the original Aeonik but introduces subtle curves at every corner and junction, shifting the register from sharp and rational to something warmer and more approachable. Eight weights run from Air to Black, each paired with a matching italic, and a variable font is included with full-family purchases. Language coverage spans Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese, with a full set of OpenType features including old-style figures, fractions, stylistic alternates and case-sensitive punctuation.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Aeonik Soft as retaining the mechanical backbone of the original while introducing gentle curves that make it friendlier and more adaptable across editorial work, brand identity, packaging, children's content and digital product design.

name: Aeonik Mono
classification_notes: Fixed-pitch companion to the Aeonik neo-grotesque family; each character set at 620 units wide; disambiguation serifs added to i, j, l and I while closed apertures and perpendicular stroke endings from the parent design are preserved. Combines neo-grotesque precision with geometric proportions.
summary: A fixed-pitch companion to Aeonik that locks the family's Swiss grotesque geometry into an eight-weight monospaced system with broad Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese coverage.
description: Aeonik Mono fits every glyph into a strict 620-unit grid while preserving the parent family's closed apertures and perpendicular stroke endings, adding disambiguation serifs to i, j, l and I. Eight weights run from Air to Black, with OpenType features including boxed and circled numerals, three arrow sets and alternates for a, f, y, J, Q, 7 and the ampersand. Language support spans most European Latin scripts, Vietnamese, Cyrillic and Greek, making it well suited to technical, interface and code-adjacent work.
foundry_blurb: CoType Foundry describe Aeonik Mono as a fixed-pitch reimagining of the Aeonik neo-grotesque, with every glyph occupying precisely 620 units of width. The broader Aeonik superfamily is trusted by global brands including Revolut, Eurosport and Alipay, combining neo-grotesque precision with geometric roundness.

name: Aeonik Fono
classification_notes: Proportionally-spaced geometric sans engineered to read like a monospace. Closed apertures, perpendicular stroke endings and elongated slab-like serifs on i, j, l and I generate the even visual rhythm of a code font. Spacing and kerning remain fully proportional, so it avoids the typesetting friction of true monospaced type.
summary: A proportionally spaced geometric sans that borrows the visual language of monospace type without the typesetting constraints.
description: Designed by Mark Bloom as a direct extension of the Aeonik family, Fono achieves the tight, even texture of a code font while retaining proportional spacing and proper kerning. Closed apertures, perpendicular terminals and elongated serifs on narrow characters like i and l carry the mono aesthetic into branding and editorial settings. Stylistic alternates extend its range further: boxed and circled numerals, character variants for a, f, y, J, Q, 7 and &, plus three sets of arrow glyphs.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Fono as a pseudo-monospace that gives the look of a mono without the typesetting inconveniences – blending elements of Aeonik and Aeonik Mono into a family that maintains the mono vibe while improving readability. Available in eight weights from Air to Black, with OTF, TTF and variable font formats included.

name: RM Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced companion to RM Neue. Uniform 600-unit character width, low contrast, compact neo-grotesque proportions. Alternate glyphs for single-storey 'a', serif-bottomed 'f', and variants of 'R', 'G' and '3'. Five weights, no italics, variable font included.
summary: The fixed-width companion to RM Neue, set on a strict 600-unit grid across five weights with variable font support and utilitarian alternate glyphs.
description: RM Mono translates the design language of RM Neue into a monospaced format, keeping the same compact proportions and low-contrast forms within a 600-unit grid. Five weights run from Light to Black, supported by OpenType alternates including a single-storey 'a', serif-bottomed 'f' and variants of 'R', 'G' and '3'. Designed to work beyond the terminal – equally at home in posters, tables and logotype work as in code editors.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe RM Mono as the structured monospaced counterpart to RM Neue, preserving its utilitarian neo-grotesque character within a fixed 600-unit grid. Weights align directly with the sister family, and the font ships with OpenType features covering fractions, superior and inferior numerals, arrows and geometric symbols alongside alternate glyph sets.

name: Aeonik
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque built on a geometric skeleton. Perpendicular terminals and closed apertures give it structural rigidity, tempered by circular bowls that soften the overall impression. Sits between the Swiss grotesque tradition and geometric sans territory – disciplined but not cold. Strong typographic texture at small sizes; expressive at display scale.
summary: A neo-grotesque with a geometric skeleton, Aeonik spans eight weights with italics across five subfamilies – Condensed, Extended, Soft, Fono and Mono – with script coverage running to over 340 languages.
description: Designed by Mark Bloom and Joe Leadbeater and first released in 2018, Aeonik applies a geometric skeleton to the Swiss grotesque tradition, with perpendicular terminals and circular bowls in tension. The family runs across five subfamilies – Soft, Condensed, Extended, Fono and Mono – each sharing the same eight-weight spine from Air to Black, with italics throughout. A 2025 expansion added Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Hangul, bringing total script coverage to over 340 languages.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Aeonik as a neo-grotesque built on a geometric skeleton, balancing mechanical precision with timeless aesthetics through perpendicular terminals and round bowls. Used in brand identities for Revolut, Eurosport and Alipay, the family has grown from its 2018 debut into a system of five subfamilies. A March 2025 update added Arabic, Hebrew, Thai and Hangul, extending coverage to over 340 languages.

name: Aeonik Condensed
classification_notes: Condensed width variant of the Aeonik family. Swiss grotesque with a geometric skeleton; perpendicular stroke terminals on 'a', 't', 'f' and 'j'; geometric roundness on 'c', 'e' and 'o'; closed apertures throughout. Available as a variable font. Developed by Mark Bloom and Diana Ovezea as a sibling to Aeonik, Aeonik Extended, Aeonik Soft, Aeonik Fono and Aeonik Mono.
summary: Aeonik Condensed applies the geometric precision and perpendicular terminals of the Aeonik family to a narrow-width form, built for headlines, posters and branding where horizontal space is at a premium.
description: A condensed companion to CoType's flagship grotesque, Aeonik Condensed keeps the closed apertures, rigid perpendicular stroke endings and geometric roundness that define the family, simply compressed into a narrower body. Eight weights from Air to Black, each with a matching italic, cover the full editorial and branding range. Variable font support allows fine-grained weight control across the entire axis, and the Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese coverage carries it across most international projects.
foundry_blurb: Aeonik Condensed distils the core features of the Aeonik family into a narrower form, offering the same mechanical precision and timeless aesthetics with a space-saving design. It pairs naturally with Aeonik, Aeonik Mono and Aeonik Fono for cohesive typographic systems, and its OpenType feature set includes discretionary ligatures, old-style and tabular numerals, fractions, case-sensitive punctuation and stylistic sets for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic characters.

name: Lock Serif Stencil
classification_notes: Serif typeface with deliberate stencil breaks applied throughout. Firmly display-use in intent — designed for titles and posters rather than body text. Part of the Lock superfamily, which roots all four subfamilies in broad-nib calligraphy. The stencil treatment pushes it into display territory despite the serif base.
summary: Lock Serif Stencil applies industrial stencil cutouts to CoType's assertive Lock Serif, producing six weights from ExtraLight to Black suited to titles, posters and experimental layouts.
description: Part of the Lock superfamily by Mark Bloom and Diana Ovezea, Lock Serif Stencil takes the sharp, calligraphically-informed shapes of Lock Serif and introduces deliberate stencil breaks throughout. Six weights run from ExtraLight to Black, carrying both formal elegance and industrial edge. Proportions align exactly with the non-stencil serif, so the two can swap without disrupting text flow — a practical consideration for mixed-style layouts.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Lock Serif Stencil as merging the sharp elegance of a serif with industrial, experimental flair through playful stencil cutouts applied to the assertive forms of Lock Serif. It sits within the broader Lock collection — a superfamily rooted in broad-nib calligraphy and industrial design — and shares proportions with its non-stencil counterpart for seamless interchangeability. Glyph alternates, arrows and circled numbers are included alongside variable font files.

name: Lock Sans
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif with calligraphic underpinning – strokes carry the subtle variation of a broad-nib pen without being overtly calligraphic. Part of CoType's Lock superfamily (Lock Sans, Lock Sans Stencil, Lock Serif, Lock Serif Stencil), developed over two years. Six-weight range from ExtraLight to Black; variable font included. Stencil companion designed for seamless interchange without text reflow. Glyph alternates for a, g, t and Q; includes arrows and circled numbers.
summary: A humanist sans-serif by Mark Bloom and Diana Ovezea drawing on broad-nib calligraphy for natural stroke variation, offered in six weights with a matching stencil companion and variable font.
description: Lock Sans is the sans-serif arm of CoType's debut superfamily, its letterforms shaped by broad-nib calligraphy in a way that reads as warmth rather than ornament. Six weights from ExtraLight to Black cover the full range of editorial and branding use, and the variable font is included with purchase. A stencil companion swaps in without triggering text reflow, and glyph alternates for a, g, t and Q give extra typographic range.
foundry_blurb: CoType describes Lock Sans as pairing the organic qualities of broad-nib calligraphy with the precision of industrial design, yielding clean, adaptable letterforms suited to corporate, editorial, and branding work. The stencil companion interchanges seamlessly without affecting text flow, and the full Lock superfamily – spanning sans, serif, and stencil variants across 24 styles – was developed over two years by Mark Bloom and Diana Ovezea.

name: Altform
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with grotesque personality. Constructed geometry provides neutrality while details in the R, t, k and optional alternate letterforms add idiosyncrasy. Available as static fonts and a variable font with a custom italic slant axis (0° to 10°). Eleven stylistic sets including single-storey 'a', wind-blown curved stems on d, i, j, l, u, y, alternate g, J, Q, R, 4, and three ampersand designs.
summary: A geometric grotesque with seven weights and matching italics that holds its neutrality in text while revealing considered detail at display sizes.
description: Altform blends the clean structure of a geometric sans with the character of a grotesque, giving it broad utility across editorial and branding work. Released in 2021 by CoType Foundry's Mark Bloom, it comes in 14 static styles plus a variable font with a customisable italic slant axis. Eleven stylistic sets unlock alternate letterforms including wind-blown strokes, a single-storey 'a', and three ampersand designs.
foundry_blurb: CoType describes Altform as solid and deceptively simple, positioning it as a sans that pairs geometric neutrality with grotesque personality, suited to editorial and branding projects at both display and text scales.

name: Lock Sans Stencil
classification_notes: Geometric stencil sans-serif; part of the 24-style Lock superfamily alongside Lock Sans, Lock Serif and Lock Serif Stencil. Six weights (ExtraLight to Black), no italics, no condensed. Ships as OTF, WOFF, WOFF2 and variable font. Stencil cuts designed to align dimensionally with the non-stencil Lock Sans so styles can be exchanged without disrupting text flow. Includes glyph alternates for 'a', 'g', 't' and 'Q', plus arrows and circled numerals.
summary: A stencil adaptation of Lock Sans across six weights, lending a bold industrial character to the geometric sans while designed to swap cleanly with its non-stencil counterpart.
description: Lock Sans Stencil applies deliberate stencil cuts to the geometric structure of Lock Sans, producing six weights from ExtraLight to Black aimed at headlines, posters and branding. Glyph alternates for key characters including 'a', 'g', 't' and 'Q', alongside arrows and circled numerals, add range for editorial and identity applications. It ships as a variable font and sits within CoType's 24-style Lock superfamily, where stencil and standard styles share enough dimensional consistency to be exchanged without visual disruption.
foundry_blurb: Lock Sans Stencil takes the refined structure of Lock Sans and introduces stencil cutouts, adding a bold, industrial quality suited to standout applications. The cuts are dimensionally aligned with Lock Sans so designers can switch between the two without disrupting text flow or layout. The typeface ships with glyph alternates, arrows and circled numbers, and is available as a variable font as part of the broader Lock superfamily.

name: Lock Serif
classification_notes: High-contrast contemporary serif rooted in broad-nib calligraphy; sharp, assertive stroke terminals sit against smoother calligraphic curves. Part of the 24-style Lock superfamily alongside Lock Sans, Lock Sans Stencil and Lock Serif Stencil. No italic styles documented. Metric-compatible with Lock Sans to allow style-swapping without text reflow.
summary: A calligraphic display serif from CoType's Lock superfamily, cut in six weights from ExtraLight to Black and built for editorial, branding and display work.
description: Lock Serif pairs sharp, assertive stroke terminals with smoother calligraphic curves drawn from broad-nib pen studies. Six weights cover everything from lightweight elegance to commanding black, aimed at editorial headers, branding and display settings. Metric compatibility with Lock Sans means the two can be swapped within a layout without disrupting text flow.
foundry_blurb: CoType presents Lock Serif as a contemporary serif that brings traditional calligraphy into modern type design. Sharp shapes sit alongside graceful curves to create a strong yet elegant tone across six weights. Together with Lock Sans and the stencil companions, it forms a 24-style superfamily suited to corporate, editorial and branding contexts.

name: Coanda
classification_notes: Strict modular geometric construction with optical adjustments for legibility. Five weights from Thin to Black; no italics, condensed or mono variants. Four stylistic sets including hairline alternates. Inspired by Wim Crouwel, Mimmo Castellano and The Designers Republic.
summary: A strict modular display face from London's CoType Foundry, drawing on Crouwel and Castellano to balance geometric construction with just enough optical adjustment for practical legibility.
description: Coanda runs from Thin to Black across five weights, each built on a rigid modular grid with occasional optical concessions. Four stylistic sets, including hairline alternates, extend its range across scales. Its character set covers Eastern and Western European diacritics, mathematical symbols and fractions, with logotypes and editorial display as its natural territory.
foundry_blurb: Coanda is rooted in the bold modular ideals of the 20th century, drawing from Wim Crouwel, Mimmo Castellano and The Designers Republic. Its letterforms follow strict modularity with occasional optical adjustments for legibility – 95% technological, 5% human – and four stylistic sets, including hairline alternates, allow adaptation across different scales and uses.

name: Orbikular
classification_notes: Bridges Transitional and Scotch Roman styles with ball terminals, high x-height, vertical stress and high contrast. Six weights from ExtraLight to ExtraBold, each with a matching italic; ships as a variable font with a continuous weight axis. CoType Foundry's first serif, designed by Mark Bloom.
summary: CoType Foundry's first serif, blending Transitional and Scotch Roman influences into a high-contrast text workhorse with six weights, matching italics and a variable font axis.
description: Orbikular bridges Transitional and Scotch Roman serifs with ball terminals, high x-height, vertical stress and high contrast throughout its range. Designed by Mark Bloom and released in January 2021, it covers six weights from ExtraLight to ExtraBold, each with a matching italic, and ships as a variable font for precise weight control. Suited to magazines, books and branding, it performs well at body sizes and scales convincingly to display.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Orbikular as a functional serif built to stand the test of time, casting a modern light on classic form. It is positioned as the right choice for anyone seeking a distinctive yet time-honoured typographic voice, with a specimen by Matt Willey of Pentagram included on full family purchase.

name: Ambit
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque with deliberate idiosyncrasies: a curly f and r, exaggerated bottom loops on c and s, and twisting legs on R and K. Three stylistic sets offer alternate letterforms including single-storey a and g, a simplified f and r suited to smaller sizes, and an alternate Q. Variable font with a continuous weight axis spanning Thin to Black.
summary: An eccentric grotesque with seven weights, defined by a curly f and r, exaggerated loops on c and s, and twisting legs on R and K – personality without novelty.
description: Launched in 2019 as one of CoType Foundry's founding typefaces, Ambit draws from early grotesque traditions while adding distinctly contemporary details. A curly f and r, exaggerated bottom loops on c and s, and kinetic legs on R and K give the design genuine character. Seven weights with matching oblique italics, a variable axis for fine-grained control, and three stylistic sets make it well suited to branding, packaging and editorial work.
foundry_blurb: CoType describes Ambit as an eccentric sans-serif that takes the charm of early grotesque type and adapts it for the 21st century. Its defining details – a curly f and r, self-curling forms on c and s, and distinctive twisted legs on R and K – run through all seven weights, each with a matching oblique and full OpenType feature support including ligatures, alternates and tabular numerals.

name: Gridular
classification_notes: Grid-based pixel display face inspired by Wim Crouwel's Architype Stedelijk. Letterforms built from interconnected pixels with slightly rounded corners on a fixed grid: lowercase at 5×7 (612 units wide), uppercase at 6×7 (714 units wide). Despite its pixel-font aesthetics, includes proportional spacing and kerning. Stylistic Set 1 provides true monospaced alternates for f, j, m, t, w, M, W. Full arrow set and specialised all-caps punctuation included.
summary: A grid-based pixel display face from CoType, inspired by Wim Crouwel's Architype Stedelijk, with slightly rounded pixel connections and proportional spacing that gives it more range than a typical pixel font.
description: Gridular builds letterforms on a strict pixel grid – lowercase at 5×7, uppercase at 6×7 – with slightly rounded corners on the connections, softening what could otherwise feel purely technical. Despite its pixel-font appearance, it includes kerning and proportional spacing, making it more versatile than most display faces of this kind. A Stylistic Set provides true monospaced alternates for key characters, and the set includes a full complement of arrows and specialised all-caps punctuation.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Gridular as a more playful take on a grid-based design, striking a balance between the decorative and the functional. It is offered free under a Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivatives 4.0 licence, covering personal and commercial use.

name: Scandium
classification_notes: Contemporary geometric sans with modestly squared curves, a high x-height, and vertical terminals. Technical in character without feeling cold or overengineered. No condensed or mono variants. Ships with variable font technology and an automotive icon set.
summary: A contemporary geometric sans from CoType, spanning seven weights with matching italics and a technical edge drawn from automotive branding.
description: Scandium is a geometric sans-serif with modestly squared curves, a high x-height, and vertical terminals – precise and assured without tipping into cold engineering. It spans seven weights from Thin to Black, each paired with a matching italic, and ships as a variable font for granular control. Alternate serif characters on I, l, i and j aid legibility in tight settings, while a bundled icon set covers automotive UI, EV charging and navigation symbols.
foundry_blurb: CoType describe Scandium as a contemporary sans-serif with open shapes and a technical vibe, developed with the demands of the automotive industry in mind. The design is self-assured and functional without feeling bland or overworked, and the foundry position it for brands across automotive, aviation, space travel and luxury watches.

name: Betatron
classification_notes: Parametric alphabet constructed entirely from vertical, horizontal and 45-degree diagonal lines. Abstract, angular letterforms that reference Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet but with a bolder, more daring sci-fi quality. Single weight; no italics or condensed variants. Free under Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivatives 4.0.
summary: A single-weight parametric display face built entirely from vertical, horizontal and 45-degree diagonal lines, taking Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet as its starting point and pushing it into bolder sci-fi territory.
description: Betatron is a free geometric display typeface by Mark Bloom of CoType Foundry, released in November 2022. Its letterforms use only three line directions – vertical, horizontal and 45 degrees – producing angular, abstract characters that reference Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet while going further in their boldness and sharpness. Available in a single Regular weight, it suits futuristic branding, display-only editorial work and experimental design.
foundry_blurb: CoType describes Betatron as bold and dynamic, inspired by sci-fi visions of the near future. The design grew from a playful Instagram experiment into a full typeface, employing a parametric grid language shared with Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet – though with sharper, more daring letterforms. Released free under Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivatives 4.0, it is available in OTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats.
